title: Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan visits farms in Punjab to improve soil health and increase farmers' income
subtitle:
'Booh Haveliyaan' shows the country a new way of stubble management amid farming without burning stubble for the last six years; Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh lauds farmers and the panchayats
Expressing disappointment over the state government's reluctance towards the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, Shri Shivraj Singh calls its implementation essential for compensating flood-related losses and other damages
Centre provides crores of rupees for agricultural machinery; the state government must ensure quality checks: Shri Shivraj Singh
body_text: The Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, today participated in a ‘Kisan Chaupal’ and interacted with the farmers at village 'Booh Haveliyaan' in Tarn Taran district of Punjab. While sitting among farmers in the fields and listening to their concerns and suggestions, Shri Chauhan commended the progressive farmers and panchayats who practice modern farming without resorting to stubble burning. He stated clearly that he had not come to hold a big political meeting, but to sit among them as a servant and understand their concerns. He urged the Punjab government to implement the ‘Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana’ in the interest of the farmers and reiterated the Modi government's commitment to pro-farmer policies and record procurement at MSP. Serving farmers is the true worship of the Satguru Addressing the ‘Kisan Chaupal’, Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, in an emotionally stated that farmers work day and night to feed the entire nation.  He said, “I am not a leader, I am a servant of farmers. Guru Nanak Dev ji has also given the same message of serving people and staying away from arrogance, jealousy and malice. “The ministerial position has not been given to satisfy any ego, but for the service of the public; and for me, serving the farmers is equivalent to worshipping Satguru Bhagwan.” From ‘Green Revolution’ to 'Khet Bachao Abhiyan' Saluting the historic contribution of farmers of Punjab, Union Minister Shri Chouhan stated that when the country faced a food crisis and had to import ‘red wheat’ from abroad, it was the farmers of Punjab who, by ushering in the Green Revolution, filled the nation's food grain reserves. But today due to excessive use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides and stubble burning, the health of our mother earth is deteriorating. Friendly insects and earthworms are dying out. He warned that if we do not save the fertility of the soil today, the coming generations will face a big crisis. Appreciating the farmers of Booh Haveliyaan and adjoining areas for not burning stubble for the last six years and adopting Happy Seeder and Direct Seeding, he said that this village has shown a new direction of ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan' to the nation. Advice to the state government regarding agricultural machinery During the interaction, progressive farmers Sardar Sukhwinder Singh (Kirtowal), Sardar Jatinder Singh (Munda Pind) and former Sarpanch Sardar Gurnam Singh put forward suggestions related to practical problems being faced in stubble management and subsidy on baler machines. Taking the farmers' suggestions seriously, Shri Chauhan assured them that he would invite them to Delhi for a detailed discussion. Meanwhile, in response to complaints regarding the machinery provided under subsidy, the Union Minister stated that the Government of India is providing a substantial sum - approximately Rs 286 crore- to the state government this year as well, for CRM (Crop Residue Management). The central government provides the funds, while the responsibility for purchasing machines and conducting quality checks lies with the state government. The state government should ensure that farmers get good quality machines and a proper arrangement for the repair in case of failures. Emphasis on ‘Fasal Bima Yojana’ and diversification Shri Chouhan stated that to make agriculture a profitable enterprise, it is essential to increase production, reduce costs, and adopt integrated farming, which includes crop diversification alongside animal husbandry, fisheries, and poultry farming. He expressed disappointments  that the ‘Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana’  has not yet been implemented in Punjab. He mentioned that he had even written to the Chief Minister during the floods, urging the implementation of the scheme so that farmers could be compensated for losses incurred due to natural disasters. The alliance in Punjab will open a new path for progress and development Speaking to the media after the event, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan reassured farmers that the Central Government procures the entire quantity of paddy and wheat at the Minimum Support Price (MSP). Furthermore, the Modi government guarantees the cent- percent procurement of pulses (tur, masoor, and urad) as well as the procurement of cotton at the MSP. Compared to the previous UPA government, the Modi government has procured significantly larger quantities, and this will continue in the future as well. **** PK/KC/RT/R
